hook: Serial 153 of the FBI's 62-HQ-83894 UFO case file is a photographic or image-format document for which no text could be extracted, forming part of a sweeping investigative record spanning June 1947 to July 1968.
why_it_matters: The 62-HQ-83894 file is the FBI's primary headquarters case file on flying disc reports and represents one of the most extensive federal law enforcement records on UAP from the early Cold War era. Serial 153 falls within a file that the manifest describes as containing newly declassified pages not previously available on the FBI Vault, suggesting this image may be among the newly released materials. Because the document is an image with no extractable text, its specific contribution to the record cannot be assessed without visual review.

key_findings.finding: This document is an image or photograph within the FBI's 62-HQ-83894 case file; no textual content was recoverable for analysis.

The parent case file (62-HQ-83894) includes photographic evidence associated with Oak Ridge, Tennessee, a sensitive Atomic Energy Commission site where UAP sightings were reported in the late 1940s and early 1950s.
The manifest indicates this file contains newly declassified pages beyond what is posted on the FBI Vault, meaning Serial 153 may represent previously withheld investigative material.

The broader case file encompasses technical proposals on potential UAP propulsion systems, eyewitness testimonies, and extensive contemporaneous media coverage — indicating the FBI tracked both physical and public-discourse dimensions of the UAP phenomenon.
The file's 21-year span (1947–1968) covers the entire Project Blue Book era, suggesting ongoing FBI involvement in UAP matters that paralleled Air Force investigations.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The 62-HQ-83894 file covers 1947–1968, directly overlapping with Project Blue Book, and FBI HQ files from this period routinely involved coordination and information-sharing with Air Force UFO investigations.
The manifest explicitly references photographic evidence from Oak Ridge, TN, an AEC national laboratory site where UAP overflights were a documented security concern.
Oak Ridge was operated under the Atomic Energy Commission, and FBI monitoring of UAP near nuclear facilities fell within AEC-FBI joint security responsibilities.
FBI HQ UFO files from this era frequently reference Air Materiel Command and later ATIC at Wright-Patterson as the coordinating body for physical evidence and technical analysis of UAP reports.
